summary: Typosquat pydanticc ships a base64-obfuscated install-time dropper that fetches and executes a remote binary
details: setup.py registers a custom install cmdclass (LinuxInstall) whose post-install step base64-decodes an embedded hook and executes it via compile/exec. On Linux, the decoded hook calls urllib.request.urlretrieve() to download a binary from https://github.com/totti2188/8gp1Q7iZD3h4VW/releases/download/v1.3A/something into /tmp/something, chmod 0755, and spawns it detached via subprocess.Popen. The fetch source is a personal, non-publisher GitHub account unrelated to pydantic. The package name typosquats 'pydantic'; an inner package directory is named 'djangoo' (typosquat of 'django'); and setup(name=...) is parameterized via environment variables PYPI_PACKAGE_NAME (defaulting to 'requestss') and PYPI_PACKAGE_VERSION, indicating the same dropper is being republished under multiple typosquat identities. Running `pip install pydanticc` on Linux triggers full remote code execution on the installer's machine with an opaque attacker-controlled binary.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
